title: Coordinatewise product representation
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, let $n\ge 0$, and let $\rho\in[0,1]$. The joint law of two sequences generated by first sampling the initial sequence from $\pi^{\otimes n}$ and then applying independent coordinate noise with retention parameter $\rho$ equals the law obtained by independently sampling $n$ coordinate pairs from the one-coordinate retention-and-resampling joint distribution and arranging the first and second entries into their respective sequences.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
